html:
The Church of the East was the Christian church of Mesopotamia and Persia, which spread along the Silk Roads as far as China and India. It worshipped in Syriac and is often called "Nestorian", a name its own members reject.

Christianity reached Mesopotamia early, but the church took shape under the Sasanian Empire. At the Synod of Seleucia-Ctesiphon in 410 its bishops organised themselves under the bishop of the Persian capital, apart from the churches of the Roman Empire. After the Council of Ephesus condemned Nestorius in 431, the Persian church kept the teaching of his school, and the split with the West became lasting.

Its merchants and monks carried it east:

  • 635: the monk Alopen reached the Tang capital, and a stone of 781 records the church in China.
  • Its bishops served the Saint Thomas Christians of South India.
  • Around 1007 the Keraites of Mongolia converted, and other steppe peoples followed.

Under the Mongols it was at its widest. William of Rubruck met its priests at Karakorum in 1254, and the monk Rabban Bar Sauma travelled from China to Rome and Paris in 1287. Gravestones near Lake Issyk-Kul record deaths from plague in its communities in 1338 and 1339.

After the Mongol rulers of Persia became Muslim, and with the wars of Timur, it shrank to the mountains of northern Iraq, Iran and Turkey. Its heirs today are the Assyrian Church of the East and the Chaldean Catholic Church.
sum: The Church of the East was the Christian church of Mesopotamia and Persia, which spread along the Silk Roads as far as China and India. It worshipped in Syriac and is often called "Nestorian", a name its own members reject.
